leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open right now and the balance is positive. The plan opens one deliberately, and this is the part to watch: the Kurucay bid puts the balance well into the negative until both sales clear. That is fine in itself — a deficit costs nothing until the instant the matchday locks — but it has to be unwound before the lock, and the window to unwind it is shorter than it looks, because the two assets being sold to clear it are both losing value every night. The sequencing exists to keep that window wide: selling Tanaka before the bid rather than after means the money is banked at today's value instead of decaying while the auction runs. If the auction is lost, there is no exposure at all and the Tanaka sale simply leaves more cash in hand.

binding_gap: The gap is quality at the back, not a hole in the formation. A legal eleven can be fielded now and will still be fieldable after both sales, so the understrength penalty is not in play at any point in the plan. The weakest fielded man is ter Horst, and he plays in the one position where there is depth to spare, which is exactly why he is the man the incoming defender replaces rather than an addition to the squad.

verdict.headline: Three actions, and the order matters more than it did yesterday.
verdict.headline_short: Three actions, and the order matters more than it did yesterday.
verdict.detail: Three actions, and the order matters more than it did yesterday. Sell Tanaka to the board now, before tonight's tick, unconditionally. Bid on Kurucay before the listing expires this morning. Sell ter Horst only once Kurucay has actually landed. The change from the last briefing is the Tanaka leg: the standing instruction was to sell him as late as the matchday lock permits, and that was wrong. Both unwind legs are falling in value every night, so the capacity that funds the Kurucay bid has a shelf life measured in ticks, not days. Held to the lock, the unwind no longer clears and the balance is negative when the matchday starts, which scores nothing at all for the whole matchday. Selling Tanaka tonight also stands on its own: he is not in the fielded eleven, so it costs zero points either way.

sell.reason: Tanaka first, independently, and tonight. He is flagged falling, he contributes nothing to the fielded eleven, and the one reason he was being kept — holding a formation open as insurance against Guirassy being unavailable — died when Guirassy was confirmed fit on three dated sources. Holding him to the lock burns a meaningful slice of the money that funds the Kurucay bid, in exchange for insurance against something that is not going to happen. ter Horst is the second sale and it is strictly conditional: he is currently in the fielded eleven, so selling him before his replacement arrives drops the eleven to ten and takes the understrength penalty at the lock. Sell him the moment Kurucay lands, and in any case well before the lock rather than at it, because he is falling too. Both sales go to the board, which pays exactly market value with no spread, rather than being listed as manager asks.

standing.name: Tanaka
standing.why: SUPERSEDES Skm5o4c (CLOSED THIS RUN) AND REVERSES ITS TIMING INSTRUCTION. Skm5o4c said "SELL HIM LAST, AS LATE AS 2026-12-04T19:30Z PERMITS". That is arithmetically WRONG and would have cost Georg the matchday. Sell him NOW, to the board, at exactly mv 5.346.604, BEFORE tonight's 21:00Z tick, and unconditionally — not as leg 2 of the Kurucay buy. THREE REASONS, in order of force. (1) THE HEDGE PREMISE IS DEAD. Skm5o4c's cost case was that while Tanaka is in the squad 5-4-1 stays legal, so if Guirassy (1920, ap 126) were still out for MD12 Georg could field Tanaka at ap 47 instead of nothing. Guirassy is FIT: Wvy7vnl established he played ~26 minutes at Arsenal, and bvb.de dated 27.11.2026 carries Kovac verbatim "Serhou hat mittrainiert und ist fuer Sonntag eine Option", corroborated by africasoccer.com published 2026-11-27T14:29:44+01:00. A hedge against an event that is not going to happen is worth zero, and it is being paid for in decay. (2) THE DECAY IS THE REAL COST AND NO PREVIOUS RUN PRICED IT. Tanaka is mvt 2 with tfhmvt -55.813. Re-measured this run, 21h-aligned, all-time: mvt 2 n=1278, mean -3,257% per tick, only 8,6% rose. kb_context's 20h bucketing gives -2,67%/13,2% and Wl3zjjo's November-only gives -4,029%/9,2%, so the honest band is -2,67% to -4,03%. At the CONSERVATIVE -2,67% Tanaka sheds ~143.000 per tick and there are SIX ticks before the MD12 lock (28.11, 29.11, 30.11, 01.12, 02.12, 03.12 at 21:00Z; the 04.12 tick falls after the 19:30Z lock). Holding him to the lock as Skm5o4c instructed burns ~805.000 to ~967.000 of unwind capacity for an ap-47 body that is NOT FIELDED and therefore contributes exactly zero points either way. (3) IT BREAKS THE KURUCAY UNWIND, WHICH IS THE PART THAT SCORES ZERO IF IT GOES WRONG. Bwdkvd1's arithmetic is correct AT TODAY'S mv: capacity 356.096 + ter Horst 7.026.840 + Tanaka 5.346.604 = 12.729.540 against a 12.000.000 bid leaves +729.540. But both sell legs are mvt 2, so that capacity DECAYS. At the conservative -2,67%: after 1 tick margin +399.000, after 2 ticks +78.000, after 3 ticks MINUS 235.000. At the measured -3,257% it goes negative after 2. A negative balance at matchday start scores ZERO for the entire matchday, so Skm5o4c's "sell as late as the lock permits" would have left Georg roughly 1.100.000 short at the MD12 lock. THE SEQUENCING THAT FOLLOWS, stated so no later run re-derives it: sell Tanaka FIRST and independently (squad 12 to 11, 1GK/5DEF/3MID/2ATT = 5-3-2, the only legal formation, all 11 fielded, zero fielded points lost, cash becomes 5.702.700); then bid Kurucay per Bwdkvd1 (spending power is floor-based at 50.149.179, so cash at bid time is irrelevant); then, ONLY once Kurucay has landed, sell ter Horst per Shz3uxr. If Kurucay does NOT land, the Tanaka sale still stands on its own merits: Georg holds 5.702.700 of non-decaying cash instead of a decaying zero-points body, with a legal fielded eleven. ROBUST IN BOTH BRANCHES, which is why it is unconditional. THE ONE REAL COST, stated honestly: at squad 11 Georg is at mgc exactly (Wtzfa28 settled min 11 / max 18), so there is no bench. An injury to a fielded man does NOT trigger -100 (he still has 11 bodies) but that man scores ~0 with no replacement available. The 5.702.700 in hand is better cover for that than Tanaka is.
